messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SLO alert -> continuous-batching p99 latency spike detected for streaming-path in prod-usw2. p95 ~ 280ms, p99 ~ 1.9s over last 5m, error rate stable. Auto-remediation not triggered. @oncall please ack.
Tilly: acked. seeing 30% of streaming requests falling into tail; dashboards show KV eviction and mixed-seq batches. starting triage.
Jay: +1, looking at scheduler metrics now. queue depth up on cont-batcher workers. suspect mixed seq length amplification.
Ena: grabbing traces. I see long pack wait times before kernel launch for a subset of requests (seq len > 1200).
Ming: on infra — no host CPU/IO anomalies. GPU util is normal-ish but some cards show high pack latency.
Tilly: customer-impact check: @Marc-CS can you confirm any customer pages?
Marc-CS: two customers reported slow chat responses in last 10m, not widespread but 5-minute window. they've been notified. ETA on mitigation?
Tilly: good. mitigation plan: 1) enable short-term scheduling fairness: lower max_batch_size for streaming lanes from 32 -> 8 (reduces packing amplification); 2) enable preemptive shed for cont-batcher for seq_len > 1024; 3) route heavy tail users to aux region fallback if available. Will roll changes canary to 2 nodes first.
Jay: agree. quick test locally with bench shows p99 drop from 1.9s -> ~420ms when max_batch_size=8 for mixed workloads. paste bench snippet:
```
# bench command (local)
./bench_stream --concurrency 128 --seq-mix small:70,medium:20,large:10 --max-batch 8
# result p99 ~ 420ms
```
Tilly: can we do a fast canary? Ming, can you patch config across 2 workers in prod-usw2?
Ming: patching now. applying config change: 
```
batcher:
  streaming:
    max_batch_size: 8
    preemptive_shed_seq_len: 1024
```
deploy-bot: deploy started by Ming -> rolling update on cont-batcher-prod-usw2 (2/12 nodes canary).
Ena: I pushed a temporary KV-cache tweak to keep hot prefixes pinned longer (reduce eviction churn).
Tilly: monitoring dashboards for p95/p99 and pack wait histograms.
Jay: seeing immediate improvement on canary nodes: p99 dropped to ~480ms on those nodes, queue wait reduced. global p99 now 1.1s (still high but trending down).
Marc-CS: customer updates: told them we're rolling a mitigation and expect improvement in <10m. they appreciate quick response.
Tilly: cool. next: after canary success, roll to remaining nodes with 30s stagger. also open temporary routing fallback for 2 high-volume tenants to aux-region. Ming can you kick that?
Ming: routing rule in-flight, will shift 5% traffic first for the two tenants, then 100% if stable.
Jay: adding a short-term metric alert to watch pack-wait quantiles and cont-batcher p99 so we catch regressions.
Ena: logs show a handful of requests still hitting >1s due to huge seq_len parsing overhead; we should consider request-size caps or early fail for extreme seqs in streaming mode.
Tilly: agreed; ticket to product for long term: dynamic padding policy + model variant fallback for extreme seqs. For now, config and routing seem to be working.
deploy-bot: rolling update progress: 2/2 canary nodes succeeded; starting remaining nodes.
Jay: full roll in progress. p99 across cluster now ~360-500ms depending on node, p95 ~ 310ms. really good.
Marc-CS: customers report recovery. closing their pages once we verify for 15m.
Tilly: assigning postmortem owner: Jay to lead. please include timeline, root cause (cont-batching scheduling + mixed-seq amplification + KV eviction), mitigation checklist, and follow-ups (routing playbook, dynamic padding, request caps).
Jay: taking it. I'll capture all timestamps and config diffs.
Ming: I'll include infra changes and the routing rule.
Ena: will attach traces and bench results.
Tilly: thanks team. leaving this thread open for 30m to confirm stability. react with :white_check_mark: when you're done.
Marc-CS: :white_check_mark: (customer confirmed).
Jay: :white_check_mark: will start the postmortem doc.
incident-bot: Alert cleared. Next steps: auto-closed in 30m if no new alerts.
Tilly: closing note — we saved a customer-impacting incident with config roll and routing. postmortem to include runbook vs canary thresholds for batcher config.
